item.title: $30 million more in pipeline for Springfield Art Museum expansion
item.description: The City Council will vote tonight on a resolution to spend $15 million in Spring Forward SGF sales tax revenue on the Springfield Art Museum renovation and expansion project, which is expected to boost local tourism, support local businesses, expand access to art education, and enrich the lives of those in the community.

item.title: Missouri reminder about expiring hunting, fishing permits
item.description: JEFFERSON CITY, Mo. — At the end of this month, all annual permits through the Department of Conservation will be expiring, and the state is reminding you to keep your permits updated. item.title: Get ready for the next "blood moon"
item.description: The Worm Moon, a full moon on March 3rd, will also be a "blood moon" due to a total lunar eclipse, which will be visible across North and Central America, west into East Asia, and can be viewed without any special tools.

item.title: Wind brings warmth back to the Ozarks
item.description: A pattern shift will bring warmer temperatures and gusty winds to the area, with temperatures rising to the 60s by Tuesday afternoon and sunny skies returning by Wednesday afternoon.

item.title: One dead, three injured in Carl Junction crash between truck and tractor-trailer
item.description: On Sunday night, a collision between a pickup truck and a tractor-trailer in Carl Junction, Missouri left one person dead and three others injured, including a three-year-old child.

item.title: Update: Car vs. train collision results in death in Barry County
item.description: A car and train crash in Barry County, Missouri has resulted in at least one injury, according to the Missouri State Highway Patrol.

item.title: Last week’s Springfield restaurant health code violations, Feb. 16-20
item.description: Routine inspections of Springfield restaurants from Feb. 16-20 revealed a variety of health code violations, ranging from improperly stored food to unclean equipment and unsanitary conditions.
